variants.headline: Business-start grant programme ends
variants.sub: Business-starting support under {programme} has come to an end.
variants.body:
The programme {programme} has ended, having paid {paid} grants and refused {refused} applications. It supported people starting a business. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that record from a judgment that either the existence or the end of a programme proves it served its purpose adequately.

A person trying to start a business is still a person whose household matters. Labour should consider public support through that ordinary perspective, rather than assume that the word 'enterprise' removes the need for fairness. A programme deserves scrutiny for its accessibility as well as its stated ambition.

We take a favourable view of {target}. The end of a programme does not erase the support recorded in its grants, and fair assessment should resist treating closure alone as evidence of inadequate conduct. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
